title: The additive vector scheme in a finite basis
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $d\geq0$, and let $V$ be a $k$-vector space with a chosen basis $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_d)$ (so it is finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]). The additive vector scheme in these coordinates is $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}k[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Its group-scheme structure [def-sc-group-scheme] is coordinatewise addition, the finite-dimensional version of $\mathbf G_a$ [def-sc-gm-ga]: the comultiplication sends $t_i$ to $t_i\otimes1+1\otimes t_i$, the counit sends $t_i$ to $0$, and the antipode sends $t_i$ to $-t_i$. The coordinate tensor product is that of commutative algebras [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. These three maps determine the group structure uniquely. For every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, the vector $X\in R\otimes_k V$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives the point obtained by evaluating $t_i$ at the coefficient of $1\otimes b_i$ in $X$. This is a bijection $R\otimes_k V\simeq V_a(R)$, carries sums to products in the additive group scheme, and commutes with every coefficient-algebra homomorphism $R\to S$. The empty basis $d=0$ and the zero coefficient algebra are included.
